localized_content.title: Mahalaya
localized_content.short_answer: For a Bengal-associated Mahalaya answer, resolve your city and accepted Bengali calendar; 29 September 2027 is only a reviewed fixture. Then use a current official programme schedule if available—or silence. The complete generic route is normal sleep and care, safe lawful listening, two labelled observance stories, optional reflection and no invented Shraddha, Chandi Path or home puja.

significance.text: Mahalaya is a Bengali calendrical and cultural threshold on Bhadro Krishna Amabasya, associated in West Bengal with the opening edge of the Durga Puja season and a recurring public-service-broadcast listening practice. It is not automatically Sarva Pitru Shraddha, Tamil or Odia Mahalaya practice, a universal dawn duty, or permission to reproduce protected programme content.
significance.scope_note: Bengal-associated transition/listening lane; ancestor, regional, Devi and current institutional procedures remain separate.

origin_narratives.title: An Amabasya threshold before the Puja season
origin_narratives.summary: The reviewed Bengali calendar places Mahalaya on Bhadro Krishna Amabasya. West Bengal's current AASAN portal describes Durga Puja as a season beginning with Mahalaya and ending with Vijaya Dashami, and briefly associates the festival with Durga's victory over Mahishasura. A separate 2027 Pitru calendar places Sarva Pitru Amavasya on the same civil date. These sources establish a calendrical and cultural threshold, not one universal ancestor rite, dawn time, Devi invocation, Ghatasthapana, home puja or portable date. The full Devi narrative and formal practice remain with their owner.

origin_narratives.title: A recurring Mahalaya public-service-broadcast practice
origin_narratives.summary: Official Prasar Bharati records show Mahalaya programming across years and formats: a special dawn Mahishasur Mardini programme in 2012, Mahalaya programmes in 2013 and 2015, and a live Mahisasur Mardini broadcast on Mahalaya in 2023. This repeated institutional record explains why listening can carry strong cultural meaning for many Bengali-associated households. It does not establish one eternal recording, script, cast, language, station, hour, posture or duty, and it does not provide a 2027 schedule. Programme text, music and audio remain protected; Devam supplies no transcript or recording and directs users to current authorised access or silence.

steps.instruction: Resolve city, local Amabasya interval, accepted Bengali calendar and Mahalaya civil day. If unresolved, do not declare today Mahalaya.

steps.instruction: Keep normal sleep, food, water, medicine and care; no dawn alarm, fast, bath, lamp, incense, altar, flower, offering, purchase or travel is required.
steps.why: The listening route must not become an invented puja.

steps.instruction: If you want audio, find a current official station or lawful stream and verify language, time, accessibility and replay rules. If no official 2027 schedule exists, use silence.
steps.why: Historical Prasar records do not establish a current programme.

steps.instruction: Use safe volume, hearing protection and a comfortable place; stop for fatigue, sensory distress, child/dependent care or device risk.
steps.why: Listening never overrides health or safeguarding.

steps.instruction: Hear the two labelled stories: Mahalaya as a Bengali seasonal threshold and the recurring public-service-broadcast practice. Do not treat either as a universal origin or puja.
steps.why: The lane can tell its evidence-backed observance history without copying protected audio.

steps.instruction: Optionally note one transition or living-care commitment, or choose silence; no belief, nostalgia, Bengali identity performance or Devi worship is owed.
steps.why: Reflection remains voluntary and non-diagnostic.

steps.instruction: Close the programme, rest, eat, hydrate and take medicine normally. Do not read dreams, glitches or later events as signs, messages, victory or ritual score.
steps.why: The generic route is complete without a result claim.

closing.text: Return to ordinary care; lawful listening, silence and no action are equally complete.

steps.instruction: Tell both observance stories and label Durga-Mahishasura victory as source context. Do not call any real person or community a demon or enemy or justify violence.
